user_request: Search unixnu.com and other devices' UniXNU projects on GitHub for the same problem and its solution
trigger: 18a1c0e6 boot: SpringBoard main thread waits on a connection port in transit inside one of 3 messages queued on launchd's service port com.apple.sessionservices (domain 1)

findings.fact: The original OS read-only shows liveactivitiesd is provided by SessionCore and its launch declaration includes com.apple.sessionservices. On iOS17 SpringBoard was seen in a synchronous ActivityKit/BoardServices request; a later boot moved past it, and the liveactivitiesd-disable candidate 7516d9be was never run.

findings.source: UniXNU/docs/devices/sirius-huajifruit.md, alioth.md, munch-erodenine.md (other UniXNU ports, iPadOS 17)
findings.fact: liveactivitiesd crashes repeatedly with SIGTRAP at one fixed PC (alioth/munch: 11 in 420 s; sirius: 17 crashes, 32 exits, xpcproxy exit 78). Sirius symbolized it as a Swift runtime trap in SessionSyncEngine under SessionCore.Daemon.workloop. Later sirius notes attribute SpringBoard and liveactivitiesd crashes to the missing display/framebuffer driver.

With a CPU renderer, liveactivitiesd/chronod/SpringBoard wait unless the AppleKeyStore state/event component is present; the fix was restoring that component and normal service startup, not disabling services.

Upstream UniXNU ships an AppleKeyStore state client handling keybag and lock-state events. The K80 iOS26 kernel instead carries iokit/Kernel/MiniAppleKeyStore.cpp; whether it delivers the lock-state events liveactivitiesd needs is not yet checked.

Official tools: Skip Setup preferences (purplebuddy SetupDone, springboard BKNoWatchdogs), lite= and disable-jobs= to isolate launch jobs, and boot-ui-focus process stack traces. The docs say to keep the services userland needs and use disable-jobs only to rule a dependency in or out.
On asteroids the official lite list itself held an XPC wait cycle; the fix was keeping only bluetoothd and coreduetd in sheng-disable-jobs.

candidate_checks_in_order: Read the root's launchd job for com.apple.sessionservices (expected com.apple.liveactivitiesd) and the current K80 iOS26 disable/lite list; confirm the job is not disabled by our own policy.
Add an observation of whether liveactivitiesd is spawned and how it exits (SIGTRAP at a fixed PC as on other ports, or never spawned).
If it runs and traps, compare K80 MiniAppleKeyStore lock-state/event handling with upstream AppleKeyStoreState/NativeKeyStoreEvents, per the UniXNU-qemu result.
Use disable-jobs=com.apple.liveactivitiesd only as an isolation test, not as the fix.
